subject: Finovus: customer storage handback and wipe certification
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@finovus.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: Customer-controlled storage — handback and certificate request

Hi Irene,

Quick one from legal/procurement at Finovus — as part of our onboarding for the Private/VPC deployment we need a documented process and evidence for the final handback and secure deletion of our tenant data when the contract ends. Specifically:

- What artefacts can Redwood provide to demonstrate a full wipe of customer-controlled storage in a VPC/private deployment?
- Do you provide a signed wipe certificate (PDF) with timestamps and identifiers we can attach to our audit?
- How do you handle backups/snapshots in the host environment and can we ensure they are not restorable after deletion?

We are on an EU region deployment and must show proof to our Data Protection Officer by the end of the month. Appreciate a short Q&A and a template if available.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Security & Compliance
Finovus Financial

Attachment: none
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@finovus.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-08T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Customer-controlled storage — handback and certificate request

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, more detail below:

1) Artefacts we can provide: deletion job IDs, storage object manifests (pre- and post-delete lists), KMS key rotation events, and audit log snippets showing the deletion workflow execution and operator accounts.
2) Yes — we can produce a signed wipe certificate with timestamps, the list of affected buckets/volumes, and the job run identifiers.
3) For Private/VPC deployments where storage is customer-controlled (customer-owned bucket/attached volumes), snapshots/backups are under customer control. Where Redwood creates managed snapshots (rare, documented in the runbook), we include their deletion in the wipe run.

I attached a short technical runbook that describes the steps and the likely artefacts we can hand over. If you like, we can provide a certificate template for legal review.

Action items: can you confirm the preferred coverage for the certificate (buckets + KMS keys + snapshots) and whether you require an independent verifier?

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Trust (Policy & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Irene / Karthik — looping in a small legal note. Procurement will want a certificate that is suitable to attach to the contract appendix. A few suggestions:

- Keep the certificate short and factual: list of resources, deletion job ids, operator initials, and timestamp (UTC).
- Add a short paragraph on scope: what "customer-controlled storage" means for this deployment and any items out of scope (e.g., developer logs retained centrally for 30 days for platform health unless otherwise agreed).
- We should offer a configurable retention window for backups (customer chooses 0/7/30 days) documented in the handoff. If the customer selects 0 days, we must ensure automated snapshot retention is disabled.

Can someone confirm whether we can sign the certificate with our standard Compliance signing process or whether legal prefers a countersignature?

Marissa

Subject: Re: Customer-controlled storage — handback and certificate request

Hi Anita — attaching the wipe certificate template and the erase runbook for your review. Below is a compact description of the proof bundle we can provide at termination for an EU Private/VPC deployment with customer-controlled storage:

Proof bundle (examples):
- Wipe certificate (PDF): list of resources (bucket names / volume IDs), deletion job IDs, deletion timestamps, Compliance signee (name + title), and hash of post-delete manifests.
- Pre-/post-delete inventory: object/manifest snapshots exported prior to deletion and after deletion (post-delete manifests will be empty for the listed prefixes).
- KMS events: evidence of key rotation or deactivation tied to the deletion window (if key is customer-managed, we record the rotation event).
- Audit logs: platform audit lines showing who initiated and approved the deletion workflow.
- Snapshot deletion confirmations: if any managed snapshots were present, confirmations that snapshot IDs were deleted.

A few notes and constraints:
- For deployments where the customer provides and owns the storage account (recommended), Redwood does not retain independent backups; our role is to run the delete workflow and record the artefacts.
- If the customer asks Redwood to manage backups/snapshots (marked in the POA), those are included in the run and we include additional snapshot deletion artefacts.
- Independent verification: we can support a neutral third-party to perform a one-time verification on-site or via cross-check of logs, subject to an SOW.

Please see the attached files for the template and the technical steps. If this looks good I can prepare a signed certificate at termination and provide the full bundle within five business days after the final deletion job completes.

Regards,
Irene

Thanks, Irene — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our DPO and procurement:

- Timing: the 5-business-day window after deletion is acceptable. Can you confirm the time format will be UTC and you will include both job IDs and the full manifest file names?
- Backups: if we choose "0 days" retention for snapshots, can you confirm there is no asynchronous platform-level backup retained in Redwood systems? We need a firm statement for the contract that remote backups are not retained beyond customer retention settings.
- EU region: can you confirm all artefacts and the signed certificate will reference the EU region and datacenter (for our audit)?

Also, procurement asked whether Redwood can add the wipe certificate to DocuSign when provided, or if we should accept it as a signed PDF attached to the final termination packet.

Best,
Anita

Hi Anita — quick technical clarifications to confirm what Irene outlined:

- Timestamps: all artifacts will use RFC3339/UTC timestamps. Certificate will include both human-readable and machine timestamps (ISO 8601).
- Job ids / manifests: we will include the deletion job UUIDs and attach the pre-delete and post-delete manifest filenames (and a SHA256 hash for each manifest file).
- Backups: for Private/VPC (customer-owned storage) the platform does not keep hidden or long-term backups on Redwood-managed infrastructure by default. If Redwood manages snapshots as part of an agreed managed-backup option, we will include explicit snapshot deletion records. We will provide a contract-friendly statement: "Redwood confirms that no recoverable platform backups of customer data exist beyond the customer-configured retention window unless explicitly configured in writing." Please review with your legal team and Marissa can provide final wording.
- EU datacenter reference: yes — certificate will state the region and the host availability zone identifiers where the resources were located at deletion time.
- DocuSign: we can provide the signed PDF; if you prefer DocuSign countersignature we can route via DocuSign but that requires procurement to share the envelope details and signer.

Next steps: 1) Anita — confirm whether you want Managed Backups disabled in the POA (default OFF for customer-owned storage). 2) If you want DocuSign, procurement to share the envelope details and signer.

Karthik
Sr. Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
